post.summary: Publish an artifact as a new release
post.description: Publishes artifactId (an uploaded bundle, or what a build produced) as a new deployment of serviceId and answers 202 with the deployment and the operation to follow. Refused while the workspace has no current plan (402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED), has an unpaid usage charge (402 PAYMENT_OVERDUE) or is at the spending cap where deploys stop (402 SPENDING_CAP_REACHED). An interrupted publication resumes on its own; repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same deployment. A bundle that carries migrations has them applied to the environment's Database before anything is published, each file as one transaction; a failing file fails the deployment with MIGRATION_FAILED, the files before it stay applied, and the previous release keeps serving. A bundle the runtime refuses for something in it (a module it imports that is not there, too much CPU while starting, its size, an unknown runtime flag, no handler, an exception at startup) fails the deployment at once with RELEASE_REFUSED, without retrying, and its log says what to change; the previous release keeps serving. Any earlier artifact of the service that is still kept can be published again as a new release, which is how you roll back; it answers 409 CONFLICT when the database already has migrations that artifact does not include. The newest ten releases of a service keep their bundle; an older one answers 409 CONFLICT until it is uploaded or built again.
post.x-mdrn-notes: The deployment and idempotency receipt are durable before acceptance. Each migration file is recorded in the database's own ledger.

post.description: Switches Database, Files (storage), Mail, Logs or Auth on for the environment. Workspace Admins only, with the product’s write scope, and the workspace must be entitled to the product (402 PRODUCT_ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED). The body is {} or, for Database only, {"engine":"sqlite"} or {"engine":"postgres"}: {} means SQLite, and an engine for any other product is 400. While the environment’s database (not deleted) uses the other engine the answer is 409 DATABASE_ENGINE_FIXED. The answer is 202 with the unfinished operation (follow it at Location), or 200 once it succeeded or failed; accepted is not done, and your app’s calls are refused until the operation succeeds. Each accepted request advances desiredRevision and supersedes an older unfinished operation of the same product. The same Idempotency-Key answers the same operation and never revives a superseded one; a different request under it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. 409 PRODUCT_OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS while a deletion of the product is still running, 409 PRODUCT_ARCHIVED while its data is archived for non-payment, 403 ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE where this stage does not serve the environment, 404 for an unknown product. Auth is the switch for sign-in: while it is off, no app address serves sign-in and switching sign-in on for one is refused (409 PRODUCT_DISABLED); each app keeps its own choice. Auth takes enable and disable only.

The answer is 202 with the unfinished operation (follow it at Location), or 200 once it succeeded or failed; an older unfinished operation of the product is superseded. The same Idempotency-Key answers the same operation.

put.summary: Connect a repository and branch to a service
put.description: Connects serviceId to repositoryId in installationId, on branch or the repository's default branch, and builds what the branch holds now; from then on every push to the branch builds the commit at its head and, when the build succeeds, releases it. Only a repository the installation lists (one you could read when you authorized) can be connected; any other answers 404 NOT_FOUND. A branch with no commit yet, or a repository GitHub refuses MDRN, is not retried: the connection's problem says so until a later push or a reconnect clears it. The repository is held by its numeric identifier, so renaming it does not break the connection. One service deploys one repository and one branch; connecting another replaces the connection. One repository may feed several services, and a push builds each of them.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Scoped to the token, the project and environment, the method and the path. Send the same key when you retry the same change.

repository.description: Ignored; accepted for older callers. The name is the one GitHub gave when you authorized.

branch.description: A branch name git allows, of letters, digits and ._-/ (no .., no empty or dot-led component, no leading or trailing /, no .lock ending, no @{). Defaults to the default branch of the repository as GitHub gave it at authorization.

put.summary: Set a variable on a service
put.description: Writes value under name, as a secret unless secret is false, and for the service's builds too when build is true; the value is never returned again. A name beginning with MDRN_ is refused, because that is where your app's product credentials live. If a release is serving, its artifact is published again so the change reaches the running app; deploymentId names that release. A release still in flight is replaced by that publication (superseded), so a missing variable can be fixed at once, unless it has already started on its database migrations or applied some: then the change answers 409 CONFLICT and changes nothing, because the serving code may not run on the database that release left; send it again once that release is live or has ended.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Scoped to the token, the project and environment, the method and the path. Send the same key when you retry the same change.

delete.summary: Remove a variable from a service
delete.description: Removes the variable and publishes the serving artifact again so the running app stops receiving it; deploymentId names that release, or null when nothing was serving. A release still in flight is replaced by that publication (superseded), unless it has already started on its database migrations or applied some: then the change answers 409 CONFLICT and changes nothing, because the serving code may not run on the database that release left; send it again once that release is live or has ended.

get.summary: Search the project environment’s application logs
get.description: Searches the logs of every service in the environment, or of one with service, newest first, in the window from and to name (the last hour when omitted). Requests, responses and exceptions are always returned; console lines below the capture level are not. level selects console lines and exceptions by level, as a comma-separated list of debug, log, info, warn and error (anything else answers 400); requests are returned whatever it is. q is at most 256 characters and matches text, without regard to case, in the items as they are answered, redacted and without anything a search leaves out, so it never matches a captured header. It is matched against the text a person reads, as it was written rather than as JSON escapes it: the message, the data logged beside it (its values, at any depth), the stack and the files a mapped stack names, the path, the service name, the request, invocation, correlation and trace IDs, numbers logged in the data (except under a name for a time: t, ts, or one holding time or date, or ending in At or _at) and the response status; never a field name, any other number, the kind, the level or the cursor. A page searched for text can hold fewer than 100 items while nextCursor goes on. Data logged beside a message is returned with it. Messages, paths, data and stacks are redacted: credential-named fields, bearer and basic credentials, cookie headers, credential-named key=value pairs and JSON members, and JSON Web Tokens. About the last six and a half days come from our network within seconds; older logs, up to the retention setting, come from the project archive, which fills within about five minutes. A page holds at most 100 items; a millisecond holding more than 100 recent items shows the first 100 of them. Pages walk the recent days newest first, then the archive newest object first: each archive page is newest first, and an object holds a few minutes of invocations, so neighbouring archive pages can overlap in time by that much. Where the walk passes from recent logs to the archive is fixed by its first page and carried in every cursor, so nothing is shown twice however long the walk takes. A walk is bound to its search (from and to as sent, level, q, service) and to the capture level and retention its first page read: a cursor sent with anything else, or after either setting changed, answers 400, and the search starts again without it, so a changed setting never makes a walk pass items over or show them twice. The window’s start as retention clamped it is carried in the cursor, so it does not move with the clock while the walk goes on. Once Logs is deleted for the environment, searches answer 403 PRODUCT_DISABLED until it is enabled again; a disabled Logs stays searchable until what it kept ages out. Every search counts as a read in Logs usage, in the UTC hour it ran.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Unix milliseconds. The window is limited to what the project keeps (its retention setting); the last hour when omitted.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Unix milliseconds. The window is limited to what the project keeps (its retention setting); the last hour when omitted.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text, matched without regard to case.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Comma-separated levels; console lines and exceptions at any of them are returned, and requests always.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pages walk from the recent days into the archive, newest first (the archive newest object first). A cursor is answered only with the from, to, level, q and service it was made with, and while the capture level is the one its first page read; otherwise it answers 400, and the search starts again without it.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Narrow to one service in the environment.

partial.description: More services could have logged in the window than one page searches (240, newest first), so the rest were not searched; narrow the search to a service. Always false for the archive.

source.description: recent: answered by our network, for about the last six and a half days (it keeps seven). archive: answered from the project archive.

retainedFrom.description: Unix milliseconds; nothing older is kept.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: sandbox or production.

get.x-mdrn-implementation-status: Deployed in the MDRN Development stage; the console uses it.

ManagementBearer.description: Management audience, team role, explicit scopes and resource ownership are checked. Workload tokens and app users cannot manage teams/billing/policy publication.

WorkloadBearer.description: Trusted server code only, scoped to its project/environment and enabled products. Users and browsers never receive it. Provider-account/Google secrets remain with MDRN. Acting-for-user operations also validate user context.

McpBearer.description: Exact resource audience and tool-specific permission required; a token for another API is rejected.

PlatformSession.name: __Host-mdrn-platform-session
PlatformSession.description: Reserved Platform console session. Cookie mutations require exact Origin and X-CSRF-Token.

AppSession.name: __Host-mdrn_app
AppSession.description: Opaque host-only application session cookie; Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain. Validated against private D1 with revocation and expiry checks. Browser JavaScript receives no service JWT or separate refresh token. Grants current-user Identity operations only, never product data.

UserBearer.description: The short-lived identity token (at most 5 minutes) the Proxy hands the app backend as x-mdrn-identity-token for a signed-in visitor. Accepted only on the current-user /v1/auth/me routes, which the backend calls through MDRN_PRODUCTS; never on product data routes and never an administrative key.

BrowserNonce.name: __Host-mdrn_preauth
BrowserNonce.description: Unauthenticated browser binding, never authority to data.

HostedNonce.name: __Host-mdrn_login
HostedNonce.description: Bound login transaction nonce, not a user identity.

CsrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
CsrfToken.description: Required for cookie-based mutations together with exact Origin validation. Bearer-only requests do not use cookie CSRF.

GitHubSignature.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
GitHubSignature.description: Provider signature of raw request; validate installation and replay identity.

StripeSignature.name: Stripe-Signature
StripeSignature.description: Provider raw-body signature/timestamp; use trusted endpoint secret and server-side customer mapping.

requestId.description: The request's id; quote it when you write to support.

operationId.description: The operation the refusal concerns, when there is one.

enabled.description: Whether sign-in is switched on for this address. It is served only while Auth is also on for the environment.

kind.description: invocation: the request or event itself. log: a line the application printed. exception: an uncaught error.

invocationId.description: The invocation this item belongs to.

correlationId.description: The identifier MDRN gives a request when it enters, carried into every service it calls. Absent from archived logs, which are stored without request headers.

path.description: The request path; the query string is never kept.

data.description: What the application logged beside the message, bounded.

deploymentId.description: The release published to carry the change, or null when nothing was serving yet.

secret.description: A plain variable is stored the same way; this records whether it is treated as a secret.

build.description: Also give it to every build of the service, secret or not, as an environment variable of the build steps. Never printed or stored with the build.

problem.description: Why connecting could not build the branch: GitHub has no commit on it yet, or refused MDRN the repository. Null while nothing is wrong; cleared once a build of the connection starts.

schedules.description: Paths MDRN calls on a timetable while this release is the active one.

name.description: The schedule’s name, kept across releases: a release that keeps a name keeps its history and next fire.

cron.description: Five fields, or @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly or @yearly, in UTC. When day of month and day of week are both restricted, a day matching either fires; a field starting with * (such as */2) counts as unrestricted for that rule, as in Vixie cron. Runs of one schedule are not kept apart: an app still working after its attempt timed out, or a retry, can overlap the next fire.

path.description: An absolute path in this app; MDRN sends a POST to it.

config.description: mdrn.jsonc as this build resolved it; null until the build has run.

migrationState.description: none: the release brought no migrations. up_to_date: every file was already applied. applied: this deployment applied at least one. failed: migration processing was refused. Earlier files may remain applied; inspect migrationOutcome, migrationsApplied and migrationWarnings.

migrationOutcome.description: What this release did to the database, kept across retries and whether or not the code was published.

artifactPrunedAt.description: In the build list: when the bundle of this build was removed, so deploying its artifact again answers 409; null while it is kept.

desiredRevision.description: The revision the request was accepted at; a later request for the same product supersedes this operation.

progress.description: The step an unfinished operation is on.

lastProblem.description: What interrupted the last attempt of an unfinished operation; MDRN retries it without anyone's help.

desiredRevision.description: Rises with every accepted request for the product.

observedState.description: The state the product last reported.

provider.description: The stage’s billing mode (BILLING_PROVIDER): sandbox, stripe_test or stripe_live; null where none is set.

planProvider.description: Who wrote the workspace’s plan: manual when MDRN granted it by hand, otherwise the billing mode it was bought through (sandbox, stripe_test or stripe_live). Null when the workspace has no plan row.

creditCents.description: Prepaid credit balance in US cents, before tax. Usage beyond the plan is paid from it first when a billing period closes.

pricedUsage.description: Whether usage beyond the plan is charged on this stage when a billing period closes.

active.description: Whether the workspace has a current plan; without one its apps are not served.

enabled.description: Whether threshold invoicing runs on this stage.

thresholdCents.description: When unbilled usage beyond the plan reaches this many US cents, it is charged at once: 2500 for every workspace. After a failed payment, the same amount of new unbilled usage refuses service where suspension is on.

unbilledCents.description: Usage beyond the plan this period not yet billed, after prepaid credit, as last rated.

paymentFailed.description: A threshold invoice is unpaid after a failed payment.

suspended.description: Apps, builds and product calls are refused until the unpaid threshold invoice is paid.

payUrl.description: The payment page for the unpaid threshold invoice: the console’s “Pay and restore”. Paying it restores an archived workspace automatically.

reason.description: Why it is archived: an unpaid usage charge (paying it restores), or a plan no longer current, cancelled or unpaid past its 3 days (buying a plan restores).

since.description: Unix seconds: when the workspace was suspended and archiving began.

deleteAt.description: Unix seconds: everything still archived is deleted then, 90 days after since.

limitCents.description: What keeping the archive may cost MDRN, in US cents: 1000.

costCents.description: What keeping what is still archived has cost MDRN so far, in US cents.

state.description: live: kept in its own database (SQLite over 5 GB, Postgres), refused while suspended.

parked.description: The move did not finish within a day and is no longer retried on its own: MDRN has been told and sends it again.

archive.description: A workspace suspended for non-payment, or whose plan is no longer current, has its Database and Files archived, kept 90 days and up to $10 of MDRN’s cost, and restored when paid. Null when nothing is archived.

capCents.description: Monthly cap on usage beyond the plan, in US cents; null when there is none, the default.

atCap.description: What stops at the cap, product by product, as the Admin chose; keepRunning unless chosen.

spentCents.description: This period’s estimate of usage beyond the plan, in US cents: the lines that could be measured, so a lower bound when a line is unavailable.

checkedAt.description: Unix seconds when the estimate was last rated.

warning.description: spentCents has reached 80% of the cap; false with no cap.

enforced.description: Whether reaching the cap stops the products chosen in atCap on this stage; elsewhere it is shown only.

observedAt.description: Unix seconds when this usage view was read; individual meters may arrive later.

meterWindow.description: Earliest and latest event time of the meters, across all recorded history.

logsUsage.description: What Logs used over the period under view (the named period, else the trailing thirty days): average GB stored, byte-seconds stored, bytes and objects written to the archive, log lines, searches and bytes they read. Shown as usage and never in the ledger; log lines are charged through the tariff (see charges). complete=false with no meters when Logs does not answer.

charging.description: Whether closed periods are charged on this stage.

creditCents.description: Prepaid credit left, in US cents.

estimate.description: Usage beyond the plan for the current billing period so far, rated against the tariff. complete=false when any source did not answer; such a line has no quantity.

included.description: Units included each period, in the meter unit.

microUsd.description: Price in micro-USD for every `per` units beyond the included ones.

perDatabase.description: Included per database rather than per workspace.

projects.description: The quantity per project, largest first, where the line’s source splits it by project; absent for a line measured for the whole workspace only (custom domains, build time).

name.description: null for a project since deleted.

unattributed.description: With projects: the part of quantity no project could be named for.

series.description: One point per UTC day of the period so far: the quantity of the project named by projectId when the line splits by project, else of the whole workspace, with each project’s share. Days add up to the quantity, except for custom domains, whose points are each closed day’s domains beyond the included ones and whose quantity is the highest of them.

day.description: Start of the UTC day, unix seconds.

projects.description: Without projectId: each project’s share of the day; the rest is unattributed.

workspace.description: With projectId, on a line split by project: every project’s quantity that day, which is what the included amount is held against.

services.description: On lines that carry services: each service’s share of the day, in the same scope; the rest names no service.

The quantity per service (deployment), largest first, of the project named by projectId, else of every project; only on lines whose source names the service: Requests and CPU time from our network’s analytics, and build time. Files gateway and Database requests on the Requests line name no service. On Postgres compute and storage, Auth’s share is the one service, serviceId auth, named Auth, with an empty environment; the rest is the databases’, and the field is absent where no Auth counts on the line. Absent on other lines measured per project only (Database, Files, Mail, log lines) or per workspace (custom domains).

closed.description: The closed period named by periodId, else the latest: what each meter charged, from prepaid credit and on the invoice.

thresholdCents.description: Cents of this line a threshold invoice already billed during the period.

quantity.description: Null while a measurement is unknown.

state.description: ownership_pending: waiting for the DNS records below. ssl_pending: ownership is proven and the certificate is being issued. active: serving. failed: our network refused or gave up; error says why. deleting: out of traffic, being removed from our network.

optional.description: The routing CNAME is required, and so is MDRN's ownership TXT (_mdrn-challenge.<hostname>) until the workspace has proved the hostname is its own: our network's verification is believed only once that record has been seen. Our network's own ownership TXT is optional, for moving a live site without downtime.

charge.description: The price accepted when the hostname was added beyond the included ones; null for an included hostname.

included.description: Hostnames included per workspace, across every project and environment.

microUsdPerMonth.description: Price of each hostname beyond the included ones.

progress.description: The step an unfinished operation is on.

lastProblem.description: What interrupted the last attempt of an unfinished operation; MDRN retries it without anyone's help.

migrationState.description: none: the release brought no migrations. up_to_date: every file was already applied. applied: this deployment applied at least one. failed: migration processing was refused. Earlier files may remain applied; inspect migrationOutcome, migrationsApplied and migrationWarnings.

migrationOutcome.description: What this release did to the database, kept across retries and whether or not the code was published.

lifecycleTiming.description: When each event of the deployment was observed, in Unix milliseconds, for diagnosis. An event that was not observed is absent. These include waits for scheduling and are not part of the stage durations in releaseTiming.

buildId.description: The build that produced it, or null when nothing built it.

Earlier files may remain applied; inspect migrationOutcome, migrationsApplied and migrationWarnings.

productionEnvironmentId.description: The id of its Production environment.
